proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and suppose that \(d_e(G)<\infty\). By the definition of \(d_e\), the element \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\). The theorem \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) identifies the fraction field of \(A_K\) with \(L\). Multiplying the covariance identity on the left by \((I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\) and on the right by \(I_n-\Lambda\) gives
\[
 \Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
\]
Thus every coordinate of \(\Omega\) belongs to \(K_G(\lambda_D)\), whereas \(K_G\subseteq L\) and every coordinate of \(\lambda_D\) lies in \(L\). Hence
\[
 L=K_G(\lambda_D).
\]

Choose \(U\subseteq\lambda_D\setminus\{\lambda_e\}\) maximal algebraically independent over \(K_G\), put \(F=K_G(U)\), and write
\[
 y=(y_1,\ldots,y_q)=\lambda_D\setminus U,
 \qquad q=|D|-|U|.
\]
Maximality of \(U\), together with algebraicity of \(\lambda_e\) over \(K_G\), makes every coordinate of \(y\) algebraic over \(F\). Therefore \(L=F(y)\) is a finite extension of \(F\), and it is separable because the fields have characteristic zero. If \(p(t)\in K_G[t]\) is the minimal polynomial of \(\lambda_e\), irreducibility is preserved by the purely transcendental extension \(K_G(U)/K_G\). Consequently
\[
 [F(\lambda_e):F]=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=d_e(G).
\]

Localize the incidence presentation first at \(S_G\) and then at the nonzero elements of \(K_G[U]\). The resulting evaluation map
\[
 F[y_1,\ldots,y_q]\longrightarrow L
\]
has kernel generated by the missing-bidirected residuals \(F_{ij}\), by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) and \(\mathrm{def:generic\mbox{-}fiber}\). For each \(a\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(g_a(t)\in F[t]\) be the minimal polynomial of \(y_a\). Then \(g_a(y_a)\) lies in this kernel and is an \(F[y]\)-linear combination of the residuals. Differentiating that identity and evaluating in \(L\) eliminates the terms multiplied by residuals. Separability gives \(g_a'(y_a)\neq0\), so the evaluated residual gradients span each coordinate covector \(dy_a\). Hence the residual Jacobian with respect to \(y\) has rank \(q\) over \(L\). Select residuals \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\) whose \(q\)-by-\(q\) Jacobian determinant \(\Delta\) is nonzero in \(L\).

There are exactly \(d_e(G)\) distinct \(F\)-embeddings of \(F(\lambda_e)\) into an algebraic closure \(\overline F\). Each extends to an \(F\)-embedding of the finite algebraic extension \(L\): adjoining algebraic generators one at a time, send each new generator to a root of its transported minimal polynomial. Every extension satisfies \(f_1=\cdots=f_q=0\) and preserves \(\Delta\neq0\), and hence gives a nonsingular isolated zero of the selected square system over \(\overline F\). Distinct embeddings of \(F(\lambda_e)\) give distinct values of \(\lambda_e\).

Partition the variables \(y\) into their nonempty child-vertex blocks. If \(r_v\) is the size of the block at \(v\), then
\[
 1\leq r_v\leq\operatorname{indeg}_D(v).
\]
The formula defining \(F_{ij}\) shows that a selected residual is affine-linear in one block when only one of its two child blocks remains in \(y\), and has block degree at most one in each of two distinct blocks otherwise. Decompose the selected square system into connected equation-block components. A nonzero term of \(\Delta\) matches equation rows and variable columns inside these components, so a component \(C\) with \(q_C\) variables has \(q_C\) equations.

Consider the component containing \(\lambda_e\). Let \(b\) be its number of blocks, \(u\) its number of unary equations, and \(m_H\) its number of binary equations. Then
\[
 q_C=u+m_H.
\]
When \(b>1\), the binary equations define a connected graph \(H\) on the \(b\) blocks. It is simple: a binary residual is indexed by one unordered pair of distinct child vertices, and the symmetric duplicate cannot occur in a nonzero determinant. When \(b=1\), there are no binary equations.

By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\), the number of isolated zeros of this component, counted with multiplicity, is at most the coefficient of \(\prod_{v\in C}X_v^{r_v}\) in
\[
 \left(\prod_{\ell=1}^{u}X_{v(\ell)}\right)
 \left(\prod_{\{v,w\}\in E(H)}(X_v+X_w)\right).
\]
After removing the unary exponents, this coefficient counts orientations of \(H\) with one prescribed indegree at each vertex: selecting \(X_v\) from the factor for \(\{v,w\}\) orients that edge toward \(v\). Fix a spanning tree of \(H\). Once the
\[
 g=m_H-b+1
\]
non-tree edges have been oriented, at most one orientation of the tree can realize the prescribed indegrees. At a leaf, the required residual indegree forces its sole remaining tree edge; deleting the leaf proves the assertion inductively. Therefore the coefficient is at most \(2^g\). For \(b=1\), the coefficient is one and set \(g=0\).

Every conjugate value of \(\lambda_e\) gives a distinct isolated zero in the query component. Components not containing the query cannot increase the number of queried-coordinate values. It follows that
\[
 d_e(G)\leq2^g.
\]
The graph \((V,D)\) has a source vertex by acyclicity: otherwise, repeatedly following an incoming arrow in the finite graph would create a directed cycle. A source has directed indegree zero and contributes no nonempty child block. Hence \(b\leq n-1\). Applying \(\mathrm{lem:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}ceiling}\) to the simple graph \(H\), after adjoining isolated dummy blocks when \(b<n-1\), gives the independent bound
\[
 d_e(G)\leq\tau_{n-1}.
\]

It remains to control \(g\) by the excess-arrow budget. If \(b>1\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
 g
 &=q_C-u-b+1\\
 &\leq q_C-b+1\\
 &\leq\sum_{v\in C}\bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
 &\leq\sum_{v\neq\mathrm{root}}\bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
 &=|D|-n+2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The penultimate inequality uses the arborescence edge entering every nonroot vertex, which makes every omitted summand nonnegative. If \(b=1\), then \(g=0\leq|D|-n+2\), because \(T\subseteq D\) and \(|T|=n-1\). Combining the two independent orientation bounds yields
\[
 d_e(G)\leq\min\!\left\{2^{|D|-n+2},\tau_{n-1}\right\}.
\]
Finally, because \(T\) is a spanning arborescence and \(T\subseteq D\),
\[
 |D|-n+2=|D\setminus T|+1\leq k+1
\]
by \(\mathrm{ass:excess\mbox{-}budget}\). Therefore
\[
 d_e(G)
 \leq\min\!\left\{2^{|D|-n+2},\tau_{n-1}\right\}
 \leq\min\!\left\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\right\}.
\]
Taking the maximum over finite-degree members in the definition of \(D_k(n)\) proves
\[
 D_k(n)\leq\min\!\left\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\right\}.
\]
For \(n=6\), the proved value \(\tau_5=24\) gives
\[
 D_k(6)\leq\min\!\left\{2^{k+1},24\right\}.
\]
The construction froze a transcendence basis and counted only isolated zeros in the component containing the queried coordinate, so no zero-dimensionality of the full generic parameter fiber was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(N\geq1\). If \(H\) is a simple graph on \(b\leq N\) labeled vertices and \(r\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^{b}\), then the number of orientations of \(H\) having indegree vector \(r\) is at most \(\tau_N\). Moreover,
\[
 \tau_N\leq 2^{\binom{N-1}{2}},
 \qquad
 \tau_1=1,
 \quad \tau_2=1,
 \quad \tau_3=2,
 \quad \tau_4=4,
 \quad \tau_5=24<64.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(H'\) for the graph on vertex set \([N]\) obtained from \(H\) by adjoining \(N-b\) isolated vertices and relabeling if necessary. Fix once and for all an orientation \(\eta\) of every edge of \(K_N\setminus H'\). If \(\xi\) is an orientation of \(H'\) whose restriction to the nonisolated vertices has indegree vector \(r\), complete \(\xi\) to a tournament \(\overline\xi\) by using \(\eta\) on \(K_N\setminus H'\). Let \(s_i\) be the indegree contributed at vertex \(i\) by \(\eta\). Every completed tournament then has the same score vector
\[
 a_i=
 \begin{cases}
 r_i+s_i,&1\leq i\leq b,\\
 s_i,&b<i\leq N.
 \end{cases}
\]
The completion map is injective because restricting \(\overline\xi\) to \(E(H')\) recovers \(\xi\). By \(\mathrm{def:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber}\), the number of such completions is \(c_N(a)\leq\tau_N\). This proves the first assertion, including disconnected \(H\) and isolated dummy vertices.

For the general numerical ceiling, fix a spanning tree of \(K_N\) when \(N\geq2\). After the \(\binom N2-(N-1)=\binom{N-1}{2}\) non-tree edges have been oriented, at most one orientation of the tree can realize a prescribed score vector. Indeed, the required residual indegree at a leaf forces its only remaining tree edge; deleting that leaf and iterating determines every tree edge. Hence
\[
 c_N(a)\leq 2^{\binom{N-1}{2}}
\]
for every \(a\). The same bound is immediate for \(N=1\), so it also holds after maximizing over \(a\).

It remains to verify the stated small values without an unsupported enumeration. Separating the factors incident to vertex \(b\) gives the finite recurrence
\[
 c_b(a_1,\ldots,a_b)
 =
 \sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[b-1]\\ |S|=a_b}}
 c_{b-1}\!\left(
 a_1-\mathbf 1\{1\notin S\},\ldots,
 a_{b-1}-\mathbf 1\{b-1\notin S\}
 \right),
\]
where \(c_1(0)=1\) and a term is zero if any argument lies outside \(\{0,\ldots,b-2\}\). Here \(S\) is the set of edges incident to \(b\) oriented toward \(b\). The polynomial defining \(c_b\) is symmetric, and a nonzero coefficient must satisfy
\[
 0\leq a_i\leq b-1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^{b}a_i=\binom b2.
\]
Thus it suffices to apply the displayed recurrence to the nondecreasing integer vectors satisfying these two elementary restrictions. For \(b=1,2,3\), it gives respectively
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
b&\text{nonzero sorted score vector and coefficient}\\
\hline
1&(0):1\\
2&(0,1):1\\
3&(0,1,2):1,\quad(1,1,1):2.
\end{array}
\]
For \(b=4\), all sorted candidates and their recursively computed coefficients are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
a&(0,0,3,3)&(0,1,2,3)&(0,2,2,2)&(1,1,1,3)&(1,1,2,2)\\
\hline
c_4(a)&0&1&2&2&4.
\end{array}
\]
For \(b=5\), the corresponding exhaustive table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrrrrr}
a
&(0,0,2,4,4)
&(0,0,3,3,4)
&(0,1,1,4,4)
&(0,1,2,3,4)
&(0,1,3,3,3)
&(0,2,2,2,4)
&(0,2,2,3,3)
&(1,1,1,3,4)
&(1,1,2,2,4)
&(1,1,2,3,3)
&(1,2,2,2,3)
&(2,2,2,2,2)\\
\hline
c_5(a)&0&0&0&1&2&2&4&2&4&8&14&24.
\end{array}
\]
Every entry is obtained from the preceding \(c_4\) row by the displayed subset sum. For example, for the maximizing vector each of the \(\binom42=6\) subsets contributes \(c_4(1,1,2,2)=4\), and therefore
\[
 c_5(2,2,2,2,2)=6\cdot4=24.
\]
Taking the maximum in each exhaustive row proves \(\tau_1=1\), \(\tau_2=1\), \(\tau_3=2\), \(\tau_4=4\), and \(\tau_5=24<64\), as claimed.

proposed.name: tau_b
proposed.def: \(\tau_b\) is the maximum prescribed-indegree coefficient defined in \(\mathrm{def:tournament\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}fiber}\) for an integer \(b\geq1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened universal degree theorem requires notation for the largest prescribed-score fiber of labeled tournaments.

proposed.name: Maximum tournament score-vector fiber
proposed.construction:
For every integer \(b\geq 1\), define
\[
 c_b(a_1,\ldots,a_b)
 :=[X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_b^{a_b}]
 \prod_{1\leq i<j\leq b}(X_i+X_j),
 \qquad
 \tau_b:=\max_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^{b}}c_b(a).
\]
Choosing \(X_i\) from the factor indexed by \(\{i,j\}\) means orienting that edge toward \(i\). Thus \(c_b(a)\) is the number of labeled tournaments on vertex set \([b]\) having prescribed indegree vector \(a\), and \(\tau_b\) is the largest such score-vector fiber.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The orientation injection and the finite dynamic-programming certificate require an explicit coefficient definition of the tournament ceiling.

obligation.attempted: I injected every simple query-component orientation fiber into a complete-tournament prescribed-score fiber, proved \(\tau_5=24\) by a finite coefficient recurrence, and combined this with the one-sink equality region, the inherited lower envelope, the exact tree boundary, the cubic transfer, and the rational quartic. These arguments sharpen the ceiling but do not construct or exclude SEM extremizers at six or more vertices in the remaining strip.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved projection-aware upper bound, the large-size equality, the inherited lower envelope, and the exact small-size table give, for \(n\geq4\),
\[
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}
 \leq D_k(n)
 \leq\min\!\left\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\right\}.
\]
In particular, \(\tau_5=24\) gives \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\). They also give
\[
 D_0(2)=1,\qquad D_k(3)=1,\qquad D_k(4)=2,
\]
and
\[
 D_0(5)=2,\qquad D_1(5)=3,\qquad D_k(5)=4\quad(k\geq2).
\]
Moreover \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) whenever \(n\geq2k+4\), and comparison with the tournament ceiling then forces \(\tau_{n-1}\geq2^{k+1}\). Thus the only unresolved pairs have \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\); the tournament-score ceiling is not asserted to be attained there.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), where \(\tau_b\) is the largest prescribed-indegree fiber of labeled tournaments on \(b\) vertices; the recurrence certificate gives \(\tau_5=24\) and hence \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\). It also proves \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) for \(n\geq2k+4\) and the exact frontier for every \(n\leq5\). The tournament ceiling is not claimed attained in the only unresolved region, \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\). Because \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the published tree class, the unconditional dispatcher retains its complete \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions at zero excess; positive excess currently receives an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental Jacobian tag and the existing efficiently reportable size-binomial ceiling. Exact positive-excess polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference are proved on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain of the conditional geometric-resolution theorem.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware tournament score-fiber upper bound and the two-sided envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\), including \(\tau_5=24\) and the six-vertex cap, the large-size equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) without claiming that the tournament cap is attained there. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the exact frontier remains between \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\) and \(\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\): the complete-tournament score fiber is only a combinatorial ceiling, and SEM branches may be lost through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The bound gives \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\), but no attaining six-vertex SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial cap because this round supplies no exact \(\tau_{n-1}\) computation and certificate within its runtime. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). On the certified event determined by a supplied valid source-prime chart, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. Their chart antecedent appears in every statement; no chart-free statistical theorem is asserted.
